marketBrief.headline: Oil backs off, but the test is only beginning
marketBrief.summary: U.S. futures pointed modestly higher in Monday premarket trading as crude retreated from a six-month high. The early relief sits alongside a Fed decision, a crowded megacap earnings slate and fresh questions about the AI spending cycle. Markets are also absorbing sharply negative early trading in Brazil after Lula's re-election; opening reports are volatile, not closing levels.
bullets: S&P 500 futures were up 0.4% and Nasdaq 100 futures up 0.7%, according to Bloomberg; CNBC reported Dow futures 209 points higher.
CNBC's premarket update put Brent at $115.02 and WTI at $101.01 a barrel, both lower on the session but still elevated.
The Federal Reserve meets through Wednesday; Alphabet and Microsoft report Wednesday after the close, and Amazon follows Thursday.
Thursday at 8:30 a.m. ET brings the advance Q3 GDP estimate and September personal income and outlays; the BLS Employment Cost Index follows Friday at 8:30 a.m. ET.
Reuters reported sharp opening losses in Brazil after Lula's election victory, including a weaker real and a temporary trading halt; those reports are not settled closing prices.
